chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar told us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, he said: Abu Nasr al-Baghdadi told me, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Maqri, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Sharih ibn Hani, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) ordered us regarding the sacrificial animals (udhiyah) that we should observe the eye and the ear, and He forbade us from the kharqaa', sharqaa', muqabala, and mudabara. The kharqaa' is the one that has a round hole in the ear. The sharqaa' among sheep is the one whose ear is split by two cuts so that it reaches the tip. The muqabala is that a piece is cut from the front of its ear, left hanging in a way that is not distinct, as if it is a zanma (a type of growth or flap). The same is said of camels: 'al-munazzam', and that hanging part is called 'al-ru'l'. The mudabara is that this is done to the rear of the sheep's ear.

key_terms.الزَّنَمَةُ: A small growth or flap on the ear
key_terms.الشَّرْقَاءُ: A defect where the ear is split open
key_terms.الْخِرْقَاءُ: A defect where the ear has a round hole
key_terms.الْمُدَابَرَةُ: A defect where a piece is cut from the rear of the ear
key_terms.الْمُقَابَلَةُ: A defect where a piece is cut from the front of the ear

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific ear defects that disqualify a sheep or camel from sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam Ali (AS) to detail the specific physical defects (ayb) that disqualify an animal from sacrifice, focusing on ear and eye imperfections. The text provides precise anatomical definitions for kharqaa' (round hole), sharqaa' (split ear), muqabala (front flap), and mudabara (rear flap), reflecting the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between natural defects and those caused by human alteration.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad, that he said: I was told by Abu Nasr al-Baghdadi, from Ahmad bin Yahya al-Maqri, from Abdullah bin Musa, from Isra’eel, from Abu Ishaq, from Shareeh bin Hani, from Ali, peace be upon him, that he said:

We were ordered by the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, with regards to offerngs, that we observe the eye and the ear, and he forbade us from (taking as offering) the kharqaa’, sharqaa’, muqabala and mudabara. The kharqaa’ is the one in whose ear is a round hole. The sharqaa’ among sheep is the one whose ear is cut in two to the extent that it falls to the side. The muqabala is that it is cut from the front of its ear, something that is left to hang in a manner that it is not obvious, like it is a zanma. It is referred to the like of that among camels as muzannam, and that hanging (part) is referred to as ri’l. The mudabara is that this is done to the rear of the sheep’s ear.
